bias_direction: I am biased toward this smoke test producing dramatic findings, because a smoke test that finds nothing reads as wasted effort and I chose the scope. That bias points at two specific behaviours: calling a capability ABSENT when it merely has a different name than I searched for, and repeating a subagent's headline claim because it is striking rather than because I checked it. I mitigated the second by re-verifying three of the sharpest agent claims against the source and by asking every agent to record ABSENT with the nearest existing surface named. I did not fully mitigate the first: the ABSENT list is only as good as the searches behind it, and .ignore hides six directories from ripgrep — a trap this session hit in reverse when it found 256 mobility leads that every prior session's search had missed.
independent_reviewer_counterclaim: The strongest objection is that this session is apparatus work, and the instrument's own acceptance criterion — one answered question, published — scores it zero. specifications 0 to 0, evidence_sources 10 to 10, no determination, no synthesis, nothing rendered. A reviewer could fairly say the repository's documented pathology is producing audits of itself, and that a seventh audit is the disease presenting as the cure. Three defences, each narrow. First, the owner asked for this specifically and as a precondition to a real batch, and CLAUDE.md rule 0 puts a live owner statement above prior ratified records. Second, it produces no new apparatus: no workplan file, no registry entry, no new script, no new table — the freeze's five prohibitions are all respected even though the freeze itself lapsed. Third, four of its findings are hard blockers on the batch the owner intends to run next, and three of those are invisible to every existing gate: a blocking check that passes having examined 111 of the wrong things, four bucket jurisdictions absent from the schema enum, and a ratified runbook whose first command names a deleted script. A fourth objection I cannot dismiss: six agents wrote to one worktree concurrently, which no convention in this repository authorises, and the only reason it is safe is that five of them were forbidden to touch tracked files and the sixth restored what it dirtied file-by-file. That worked, and it was not guaranteed to.
